"""ml-cil-replay-strategy: the replay memory and the replay objective of a class-incremental learner.

Protocol (one draw = one whole class-incremental stream).  The server draws a
class order, cuts the classes into ``n_contexts`` disjoint contexts and then
walks the stream, ONE CONTEXT PER QUERY: query ``phase="context"`` carries
that context's training rows (``x`` ``(n_c, 512)`` frozen features in a
salted basis, ``y`` ``(n_c,)`` their labels, ``rows`` ``(n_c,)`` their index
in the stream) and nothing of any other context; the client trains on it for
``steps`` optimisation steps and answers ``{"ok": 1}``.  After the last
context, query ``phase="predict"`` carries the held-out test rows of EVERY
class seen and the client answers ``labels`` ``(m,)``.  The server scores the
FINAL AVERAGE ACCURACY -- the mean over contexts of the accuracy on that
context's test rows -- which is the class-IL number of the continual-learning
literature.  The test labels, the class order and the context of every test
row never leave this process.

THE REPLAY MEMORY IS THE SERVER'S.  A client that kept every context it was
sent would not be solving the problem, so the episodic memory is not a Python
object inside the client: it is a fixed array of ``buffer_size`` SLOTS held
here, and the client reaches it through three whitelisted calls --
``buffer_write`` (put stream row ``r`` -- one the client has already been
sent, or ``-1`` to empty the slot -- into slot ``s``, with an auxiliary
vector of ``extra_dim`` floats), ``buffer_read`` (give me the features, labels, contexts and
auxiliary vectors of these slots) and ``buffer_state`` (what is in the
memory: per slot, the stream row, its label, its context).  The budget of the
spec is therefore structural rather than checked after the fact: the memory
holds at most ``buffer_size`` rows of the stream, each with ``extra_dim =
n_classes`` floats of whatever the strategy wants to keep about it (the
stored logits of DER, a herding rank, an age), and nothing else survives a
context boundary except the network and whatever the strategy keeps on
itself.  What this does NOT enforce -- said plainly, as in the rest of this
lab -- is that the client forgets a context after it is trained on: the
editable block is arbitrary code in its own process, so a submission that
hoards the contexts it was sent can train on all of them jointly.  The
harness makes the honest path the natural one (the driver keeps nothing, the
memory is real and finite, each context is sent once) and the wall-clock
budget keeps the room for anything else small; a submission is read with that
in mind.

Data.  The frozen CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 of ``build_data.py``, its 512-d
post-average-pool features, and two labelled pools: the CIFAR-10
train/test features (10 classes, the classic Split-CIFAR-10 stream) and the
CIFAR-100 test features (100 classes at 100 rows each, from which a longer
stream of 20 classes with a few dozen rows per class is cut -- a
Split-CIFAR-100-like regime on a TRANSFERRED representation, since the frozen
network never saw those classes).  Every draw is a SALTED VIEW of the baked
features (``lab.rotate_features``: per-draw column standardisation, a
Haar-random orthogonal change of basis, isotropic Gaussian noise, salted
subsampling and row shuffling), computed on the train and test blocks
TOGETHER so both sides of a draw see the same map.

The noise of that view is a difficulty knob, not decoration.  The frozen
network was trained on CIFAR-10, so its CIFAR-10 features are separable to
99.9 % and a stream built on them raw would be won by any rule that stores a
few rows per class and takes the nearest class mean -- the task would measure
nothing.  The noise puts the joint (offline) accuracy of the very network the
driver trains into a regime where the replay OBJECTIVE has to do work, and the
server measures exactly that as a permanent diagnostic: ``offline_acc`` is the
accuracy of the same architecture, optimiser and step budget trained on the
whole stream at once, and ``offline_acc_lo`` / ``offline_acc_hi`` are the same
number at half and twice the setting's noise.

What the salted view does NOT do: hide which stored row a sent row is.  A
client that could read the stored pools could match the rows it receives
(pairwise distances are rotation invariant) and read off the test labels,
which is exactly the truth.  That is why the pools are NOT readable: every
array under ``/opt/mlvision-lab-data`` is encrypted at image build
(``build_data.py``), the key exists at run time only in the task's
per-setting script -- present at verification time, never during the agent's
phase -- and the guard hands it to this evaluator process alone while the
client runs as an unprivileged uid that cannot read the evaluator's
environment or memory, the script directory, or the blobs (mode 0600 root).
The rendered task also has no network in any phase (``harbor.allow_internet:
false``).

The truth of a draw -- the class of every held-out test row -- is a property
of a real labelled dataset the client cannot re-derive, not a label a
disclosed generator would hand back: reading this module tells a client the
FAMILY of the stream (a class-incremental split of a labelled pool) and
nothing about the draw, since the class order, the rows, the basis and the
noise are all salted.

A parameter given as a two-element list ``[lo, hi]`` is a RANGE: every draw
samples its own value with the salted rng (integers inclusive, floats
uniform).  The hidden setting is specified this way, EXCEPT for the number of
classes and the number of contexts, which fix the chance level and therefore
the scale of the accuracy: they are points in every setting so that the
metric of the hidden setting is comparable with the visible ones.
"""
import sys

import numpy as np

import mlvision_lab as lab


# The evaluator runs ``mlvision_lab.py`` as ``__main__`` (the guard starts a
# temp copy of the file), while this module imports the workspace copy as
# ``mlvision_lab``: the two module objects are distinct, so ``lab.ProtocolError``
# is NOT the class ``Session.query``'s ``except ProtocolError`` catches, and
# refusing a client call with it would kill the evaluator instead of sending
# the client an ``error`` message.  Raising a class derived from BOTH is caught
# either way; the tuple collapses to one base outside the guard.
_PE_BASES = tuple(dict.fromkeys(
    c for c in (lab.ProtocolError, getattr(sys.modules.get("__main__"), "ProtocolError", None))
    if isinstance(c, type) and issubclass(c, Exception)))


class ProtocolError(*(_PE_BASES or (Exception,))):
    """A client message that violates this task's interface, refused gracefully."""


CUSTOM = "custom_replay.py"
# Seconds per setting for the client (the server enforces the same deadline).
# A cell is ``reps`` whole streams: for each, ``n_contexts * steps``
# optimisation steps of a 512-256-C MLP on minibatches of 32 current and 32
# replayed rows, each step costing one ``buffer_read`` and one
# ``buffer_write`` round trip on the unix socket, plus the server's own
# offline reference at three noise levels on the first draw.  Set from the
# measured wall-clock of the slowest baseline cell (8 vCPU per container, the
# nine setting x seed cells of a baseline concurrent, one thread per process),
# with margin.
BUDGET = 400

_DIM = 512

# The fixed training recipe.  It is the experimental control of the task --
# the driver in the template runs exactly this, and the offline reference
# below trains the same network the same way on the whole stream at once, so
# that ``offline_acc`` is the joint-training ceiling of the recipe rather
# than of some other one.
RECIPE = {"hidden": 256, "lr": 0.03, "momentum": 0.9, "weight_decay": 0.0}

MAX_SLOTS_PER_CALL = 4096       # rows one buffer_read / buffer_write may touch

ENVS = {
    # pool: which labelled feature pools the stream is cut from ("cifar10" =
    # the frozen model's own training classes, train and test pools disjoint;
    # "cifar100_test" = 100 classes of 100 rows the frozen model never saw,
    # split per class per draw); n_classes / classes_per_context: the class-IL
    # split (n_contexts = n_classes / classes_per_context); buffer_size: slots
    # of episodic memory, the axis of this task; n_train_per_class /
    # n_test_per_class: rows drawn per class; noise: sd of the isotropic noise
    # added to the features after the rotation, relative to their mean column
    # sd (the difficulty knob, see the module docstring); steps / batch /
    # replay_batch: optimisation steps per context and the two minibatch
    # sizes; reps: independent streams averaged (each with its own classes,
    # class order, rows, basis and noise).
    "cifar10-buf200": {"pool": "cifar10", "n_classes": 10, "classes_per_context": 2,
                       "buffer_size": 200, "n_train_per_class": 700, "n_test_per_class": 300,
                       "noise": 2.5, "steps": 200, "batch": 32, "replay_batch": 32, "reps": 4},
    "cifar10-buf500": {"pool": "cifar10", "n_classes": 10, "classes_per_context": 2,
                       "buffer_size": 500, "n_train_per_class": 700, "n_test_per_class": 300,
                       "noise": 2.5, "steps": 200, "batch": 32, "replay_batch": 32, "reps": 4},
    # Hidden: the far end of the same axis -- twice the contexts, a
    # TRANSFERRED representation (classes the frozen network never saw), a few
    # dozen rows per class and a memory of only a handful of rows per class,
    # with the memory, the rows per class and the observation noise all drawn
    # from ranges.  The class count and the context count are pinned: they set
    # the chance level, hence the scale of the accuracy.
    "long-stream": {"pool": "cifar100_test", "n_classes": 20, "classes_per_context": 2,
                    "buffer_size": [160, 300], "n_train_per_class": [55, 70],
                    "n_test_per_class": 30, "noise": [1.0, 2.0], "steps": 120,
                    "batch": 32, "replay_batch": 32, "reps": 6},
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the stream (its labels are the truth; they never leave this file)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _load(spec):
    """Decrypt the setting's feature pools into this process's memory (nothing is written back)."""
    if spec["pool"] == "cifar10":
        return {"shared": False,
                "x_train": lab.load_array("features/cifar10_train_feats.npy"),
                "y_train": np.asarray(lab.load_array("features/cifar10_train_labels.npy"), np.int64),
                "x_test": lab.load_array("features/cifar10_test_feats.npy"),
                "y_test": np.asarray(lab.load_array("features/cifar10_test_labels.npy"), np.int64)}
    name = str(spec["pool"])
    x = lab.load_array(f"features/{name}_feats.npy")
    y = np.asarray(lab.load_array(f"features/{name}_labels.npy"), np.int64)
    # One pool: the train and test rows of a class are cut from it per draw,
    # disjointly (there is no separate test split for these classes).
    return {"shared": True, "x_train": x, "y_train": y, "x_test": x, "y_test": y}


def _draw(spec, p, rng, pools):
    """One salted class-incremental stream: the contexts the client sees and the private test labels."""
    n_classes, cpt = int(p["n_classes"]), int(p["classes_per_context"])
    n_ctx = n_classes // cpt
    n_tr, n_te = int(p["n_train_per_class"]), int(p["n_test_per_class"])

    pool_classes = np.unique(pools["y_train"])
    if len(pool_classes) < n_classes:
        raise ValueError(f"pool has {len(pool_classes)} classes, need {n_classes}")
    # The class ORDER is salted: which classes the stream uses and in which
    # context each of them arrives changes from draw to draw, as the
    # class-order randomisation of the continual-learning papers does.
    chosen = pool_classes[rng.permutation(len(pool_classes))[:n_classes]]

    tr_blocks, te_blocks, tr_lab, te_lab = [], [], [], []
    for new_label, cls in enumerate(chosen):
        if pools["shared"]:
            idx = np.flatnonzero(pools["y_train"] == cls)
            perm = rng.permutation(len(idx))
            take_tr = min(n_tr, max(0, len(idx) - n_te))
            sel_tr, sel_te = idx[perm[:take_tr]], idx[perm[take_tr:take_tr + n_te]]
        else:
            idx_tr = np.flatnonzero(pools["y_train"] == cls)
            idx_te = np.flatnonzero(pools["y_test"] == cls)
            sel_tr = rng.choice(idx_tr, size=min(n_tr, len(idx_tr)), replace=False)
            sel_te = rng.choice(idx_te, size=min(n_te, len(idx_te)), replace=False)
        tr_blocks.append(np.asarray(pools["x_train"][np.sort(sel_tr)], np.float64))
        te_blocks.append(np.asarray(pools["x_test"][np.sort(sel_te)], np.float64))
        tr_lab.append(np.full(len(sel_tr), new_label, np.int64))
        te_lab.append(np.full(len(sel_te), new_label, np.int64))

    x_tr, y_tr = np.concatenate(tr_blocks), np.concatenate(tr_lab)
    x_te, y_te = np.concatenate(te_blocks), np.concatenate(te_lab)
    n_train_rows = len(x_tr)

    # One map for both blocks: standardise, Haar rotation, then the noise
    # (drawn separately so the offline reference can re-add it at other
    # levels on the same basis).
    base = lab.rotate_features(rng, np.concatenate([x_tr, x_te]), noise=0.0, standardize=True)
    view = lab.add_noise(rng, base, float(p["noise"]))
    x_tr, x_te = view[:n_train_rows], view[n_train_rows:]

    # Rows of a context are shuffled; contexts are contiguous blocks of the
    # stream in arrival order, which is what ``rows`` indexes.
    order = []
    for c in range(n_ctx):
        block = np.flatnonzero((y_tr >= c * cpt) & (y_tr < (c + 1) * cpt))
        order.append(block[rng.permutation(len(block))])
    order = np.concatenate(order)
    x_tr, y_tr = x_tr[order], y_tr[order]
    ctx_of_row = y_tr // cpt
    bounds = np.searchsorted(ctx_of_row, np.arange(n_ctx + 1))

    perm_te = rng.permutation(len(y_te))
    x_te, y_te = x_te[perm_te], y_te[perm_te]

    return {"x_stream": x_tr.astype(np.float32), "y_stream": y_tr, "ctx_of_row": ctx_of_row,
            "bounds": bounds, "n_ctx": n_ctx, "cpt": cpt, "n_classes": n_classes,
            "x_test": x_te.astype(np.float32), "y_test": y_te, "base": base,
            "n_train_rows": n_train_rows, "order": order, "perm_test": perm_te}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the server-side episodic memory (the enforced budget)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class _Memory:
    """``capacity`` slots, each holding one row of the stream plus ``extra_dim`` floats."""

    def __init__(self, capacity, extra_dim, draw):
        self.capacity, self.extra_dim = int(capacity), int(extra_dim)
        self.row = np.full(self.capacity, -1, np.int64)
        self.extra = np.zeros((self.capacity, self.extra_dim), np.float32)
        self.draw = draw
        self.released = 0            # rows of the stream sent to the client so far
        self.writes = 0

    # -- validation helpers ------------------------------------------------
    def _slots(self, msg, name="slots"):
        s = np.asarray(msg.get(name))
        if s.ndim != 1 or not np.issubdtype(s.dtype, np.integer):
            raise ProtocolError(f"{name} must be a 1-d integer array")
        if len(s) == 0 or len(s) > MAX_SLOTS_PER_CALL:
            raise ProtocolError(f"{name} must hold between 1 and {MAX_SLOTS_PER_CALL} entries")
        if s.min() < 0 or s.max() >= self.capacity:
            raise ProtocolError(f"{name} must take values in [0, {self.capacity})")
        return s.astype(np.int64)

    # -- the three whitelisted calls ---------------------------------------
    def write(self, msg):
        # A slot may appear more than once in one call (a reservoir can pick
        # the same slot twice inside a minibatch): the last entry wins, as it
        # would if the rows had been written one at a time.
        slots = self._slots(msg)
        rows = np.asarray(msg.get("rows"))
        if rows.shape != slots.shape or not np.issubdtype(rows.dtype, np.integer):
            raise ProtocolError("buffer_write: rows must be an integer array of the shape of slots")
        rows = rows.astype(np.int64)
        if rows.min() < -1 or rows.max() >= self.released:
            raise ProtocolError("buffer_write: rows must be rows of a context already sent, "
                                f"i.e. in [0, {self.released}), or -1 to empty the slot")
        extras = msg.get("extra")
        if extras is None:
            ex = np.zeros((len(slots), self.extra_dim), np.float32)
        else:
            try:
                ex = lab.check_array(extras, (len(slots), self.extra_dim), name="buffer_write: extra")
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise ProtocolError(str(exc)) from None
            ex = ex.astype(np.float32)
        self.row[slots] = rows
        self.extra[slots] = np.where((rows >= 0)[:, None], ex, 0.0)
        self.writes += int(np.sum(rows >= 0))
        return {"stored": int(np.sum(self.row >= 0))}

    def read(self, msg):
        slots = self._slots(msg)
        rows = self.row[slots]
        if np.any(rows < 0):
            raise ProtocolError("buffer_read: every slot read must have been written")
        d = self.draw
        return {"x": d["x_stream"][rows], "y": d["y_stream"][rows],
                "context": d["ctx_of_row"][rows], "row": rows,
                "extra": self.extra[slots].copy()}

    def state(self, _msg):
        rows = self.row
        filled = rows >= 0
        d = self.draw
        y = np.where(filled, d["y_stream"][np.maximum(rows, 0)], -1).astype(np.int64)
        ctx = np.where(filled, d["ctx_of_row"][np.maximum(rows, 0)], -1).astype(np.int64)
        return {"row": rows.copy(), "y": y, "context": ctx, "stored": int(filled.sum())}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the offline reference (identical recipe, the whole stream at once)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _train_joint(rng, x_tr, y_tr, x_te, n_classes, steps, batch):
    """Train the driver's network on the WHOLE stream at once and return its test predictions."""
    import torch
    from torch import nn

    torch.set_num_threads(lab.cpu_threads())
    torch.manual_seed(int(rng.integers(1 << 31)))
    model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(x_tr.shape[1], RECIPE["hidden"]), nn.ReLU(),
                          nn.Linear(RECIPE["hidden"], int(n_classes)))
    opt = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=RECIPE["lr"], momentum=RECIPE["momentum"],
                          weight_decay=RECIPE["weight_decay"])
    X = torch.as_tensor(np.ascontiguousarray(x_tr, np.float32))
    Y = torch.as_tensor(np.ascontiguousarray(y_tr, np.int64))
    loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(int(rng.integers(1 << 31)))
    model.train()
    for _ in range(int(steps)):
        sel = torch.randint(len(X), (int(batch),), generator=gen)
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss_fn(model(X[sel]), Y[sel]).backward()
        opt.step()
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        pred = model(torch.as_tensor(np.ascontiguousarray(x_te, np.float32))).argmax(1).numpy()
    return pred


def _offline(rng, draw, p, noise_scale):
    """``offline_acc`` at ``noise_scale`` x the setting's noise: same recipe, no forgetting."""
    view = lab.add_noise(rng, draw["base"], float(p["noise"]) * float(noise_scale))
    n = draw["n_train_rows"]
    # ``base`` is the pre-shuffle concatenation of the train and test blocks:
    # apply the draw's own permutations so the rows line up with the labels
    # the client's stream and the scored test set carry.
    x_tr = view[:n][draw["order"]]
    x_te = view[n:][draw["perm_test"]]
    pred = _train_joint(rng, x_tr, draw["y_stream"], x_te, draw["n_classes"],
                        draw["n_ctx"] * int(p["steps"]), int(p["batch"]))
    return float(np.mean(pred == draw["y_test"]))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# protocol
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def serve(spec, seed, rng, sess):
    pools = _load(spec)
    accs, firsts, lasts, shares, writes = [], [], [], [], []
    off = {0.5: float("nan"), 1.0: float("nan"), 2.0: float("nan")}

def _map_at_r(emb, labels):
    """MAP@R, R-precision and precision@1 of a labelled embedding set.

    Musgrave, Belongie & Lim (ECCV 2020), section 3.2: for every row as a
    query against all the others, R is the number of remaining rows of its
    class, and

        AP@R = (1 / R) * sum_{i=1..R} P(i) * rel(i)

    class and ``P(i)`` the precision among the first i.  Dividing by R
    rather than by the number of retrieved correct rows is what makes the
    measure penalise a query whose class is not retrieved at all, which is
    the property the paper argues for over Recall@1.  R-precision is
    ``(number correct in the first R) / R``; precision@1 is the accuracy of
    the single nearest neighbour.  Cosine similarity on L2-normalised rows.
    """
    emb = np.ascontiguousarray(emb, np.float32)
    norms = np.linalg.norm(emb, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    emb = emb / np.maximum(norms, 1e-12)

    n = len(labels)

    R = (counts[labels] - 1).astype(np.int64)
    kmax = int(max(R.max(), 1))
    ranks = np.arange(1, kmax + 1, dtype=np.float64)
    ap = np.zeros(n)
    rp = np.zeros(n)
    p1 = np.zeros(n)
    for start in range(0, n, _CHUNK):
        stop = min(start + _CHUNK, n)
        sim = emb[start:stop] @ emb.T
        # A row never retrieves itself.
        sim[np.arange(stop - start), np.arange(start, stop)] = -np.inf
        row = np.arange(stop - start)[:, None]
        if kmax < sim.shape[1]:
            part = np.argpartition(-sim, kmax - 1, axis=1)[:, :kmax]
        else:
            part = np.tile(np.arange(sim.shape[1]), (stop - start, 1))
        order = np.argsort(-sim[row, part], axis=1, kind="stable")
        idx = part[row, order]
        correct = (labels[idx] == labels[start:stop, None])
        keep = np.arange(kmax)[None, :] < R[start:stop, None]
        hit = (correct & keep).astype(np.float64)
        prec = np.cumsum(correct, axis=1) / ranks
        denom = np.maximum(R[start:stop], 1).astype(np.float64)

def _corrupt(rng, X, y, params):

    concentrated on the borderline rows.

    WHERE a corrupted row goes: a class other than the true one, drawn from a
    CONFUSION MATRIX built from the class centroids -- ``T[i][j] ~

    equally likely (the class-conditional case).  With ``gamma > 0`` the rows
    are ranked inside their class by the cosine margin between their own
    class centroid and the nearest other one, and the flip probability is
    proportional to ``(1 - rank) ** gamma``, rescaled to mean ``noise_rate``
    and clipped at 0.9: the corruption then concentrates on the borderline
    rows, the instance-dependent regime (Xia et al., *Part-dependent Label

    function runs here and nowhere else.

        other[rows, y] = -np.inf
        margin = S[rows, y] - other.max(1)
        rank = np.empty(n)                          # within-class rank of the margin, in (0, 1)
        for c in range(C):
            m = np.where(y == c)[0]
            if len(m) == 0:

            rank[m[order]] = (np.arange(len(m)) + 0.5) / len(m)

    prob = np.clip(float(params["noise_rate"]) * w / max(float(w.mean()), 1e-12), 0.0, 0.9)

# protocol
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def serve(spec, seed, rng, sess):

            # head fitted on the noisy labels recovers the clean ones, and how
            # far it memorises the corrupted ones.
            logits, _ = _train_head(rng, view, np.arange(n), noisy, False)

            "noise_rate": float(np.mean(rates)), "train_calls": float(np.mean(calls_used)),

material a transition-matrix estimator is allowed in this problem -- a

``result`` with ``transition`` ``(C, C)``, row ``i`` = the conditional
distribution of the noisy label given clean class ``i``,
``T[i, j] = P(noisy = j | clean = i)``.  The server projects the answer
onto the row-stochastic simplex (negatives clipped, rows renormalised, an
all-zero row replaced by the uniform row), scores
``||T_hat - T||_1 / C`` against the transition matrix it drew, and trains a
forward-corrected head with the submitted matrix to report the accuracy that
matrix buys on held-out CLEAN labels.  The clean labels, the drawn matrix
and the per-class noise rates never leave this process.

baked into the image (``build_data.py``); the clean labels are the ones the
feature pool carries.  Every draw is a SALTED VIEW (the public-data leak
rule of ``mlvision_lab``): the pooled features are standardised, mapped by a
Haar-random orthonormal frame into a ``dim``-dimensional subspace, and
isotropic Gaussian noise of a fixed multiple of the feature scale is added.

problem the one the literature studies: the clean posterior P(y | x) is
genuinely soft (a linear probe on the view is far from perfect), so no
method can recover the clean labels of individual rows and read the matrix
off a confusion table -- the estimator has to deal with the classifier's own
error, which is exactly what anchor points, T-Revision, Dual-T and
volume minimisation disagree about.

client that could read the baked feature pool and the clean labels next to

noisy linear image of a stored row, and distances are approximately
preserved) and count the matrix exactly.  That is why the pools are NOT
readable: every array under ``/opt/mlvision-lab-data`` is encrypted at image

directory root-only), the client runs as an unprivileged uid that can read

the client could re-derive by re-running the generator: reading this module

in the literature anyway) and nothing about the matrix drawn, whose

    # held-out CLEAN-labelled rows kept here for the forward-correction
    # diagnostic; dim: dimension of the salted feature view; noise: sd of the
    # isotropic noise added to it, as a multiple of the view's mean column sd
    # (the difficulty knob: it sets how soft the clean posterior is);
    # rate_lo/rate_hi: range the per-class noise rate eps_i is drawn from;
    # n_targets: how many wrong classes carry the bulk of a row's noise mass;

    # draws averaged, each with its own frame, noise, subsample and matrix.
    "dense-random": {"pool": _POOL, "n_train": 10000, "n_test": 4000, "dim": 128, "noise": 5.0,
                     "rate_lo": 0.15, "rate_hi": 0.55, "n_targets": 9, "conc": 1.0, "alpha": 1.0,
                     "reps": 8},
    "sparse-flip": {"pool": _POOL, "n_train": 10000, "n_test": 4000, "dim": 128, "noise": 5.0,
                    "rate_lo": 0.20, "rate_hi": 0.50, "n_targets": 1, "conc": 0.85, "alpha": 1.0,
                    "reps": 8},
    # Hidden: intermediate sparsity, with every parameter drawn per draw.
    "mixed-structure": {"pool": _POOL, "n_train": [7000, 12000], "n_test": 4000,
                        "dim": [96, 160], "noise": [3.5, 7.0], "rate_lo": [0.12, 0.25],
                        "rate_hi": [0.40, 0.58], "n_targets": [1, 4], "conc": [0.60, 0.95],
                        "alpha": [0.7, 4.0], "reps": 8},
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# small multinomial-logistic solvers (numpy; the client has its own copy of
# the plain one in the template's FIXED region)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _softmax(Z):
    Z = Z - Z.max(1, keepdims=True)
    E = np.exp(Z)
    return E / E.sum(1, keepdims=True)


def _design(X):
    return np.hstack([np.asarray(X, np.float64), np.ones((len(X), 1))])


def _adam(grad_fn, shape, epochs=_EPOCHS, lr=_LR):
    W = np.zeros(shape)
    m, v = np.zeros_like(W), np.zeros_like(W)
    for t in range(1, int(epochs) + 1):
        g = grad_fn(W)
        m = 0.9 * m + 0.1 * g
        v = 0.999 * v + 0.001 * g * g
        W -= lr * (m / (1 - 0.9 ** t)) / (np.sqrt(v / (1 - 0.999 ** t)) + 1e-8)
    return W


def _fit_ce(X, y, n_classes, epochs=_EPOCHS, lr=_LR, wd=_WD):
    """Multinomial logistic head on hard labels (full-batch Adam)."""
    n = len(X)
    Y = np.zeros((n, n_classes))
    Y[np.arange(n), np.asarray(y, np.int64)] = 1.0

    def grad(W):
        return X.T @ (_softmax(X @ W) - Y) / n + wd * W

    return _adam(grad, (X.shape[1], n_classes), epochs, lr)


def _fit_forward(X, y_noisy, T, epochs=_EPOCHS, lr=_LR, wd=_WD):
    """Head trained with the forward correction of Patrini et al. (2017) under ``T``.

    Loss = cross entropy of ``softmax(XW) @ T`` against the noisy labels, so
    the head is pushed towards the CLEAN posterior when ``T`` is right.
    """
    n, C = len(X), T.shape[0]
    Tc = np.clip(np.asarray(T, np.float64), 1e-6, None)
    idx, yn = np.arange(n), np.asarray(y_noisy, np.int64)

    def grad(W):
        P = _softmax(X @ W)
        Q = np.clip(P @ Tc, 1e-12, None)
        g = -Tc[:, yn].T / Q[idx, yn][:, None]          # dL/dp
        G = P * (g - (P * g).sum(1, keepdims=True))     # through the softmax
        return X.T @ G / n + wd * W

    return _adam(grad, (X.shape[1], C), epochs, lr)


def _probe_acc(Xtr, ytr, Xte, yte, n_classes):
    """Accuracy on held-out clean labels of a head trained on CLEAN labels (difficulty diagnostic)."""
    W = _fit_ce(Xtr, ytr, n_classes)
    return lab.accuracy(yte, np.argmax(Xte @ W, 1))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the draw
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _draw_transition(rng, C, p):
    """A row-stochastic, diagonally dominant class-conditional noise matrix.

    Row ``i``: the clean class keeps ``1 - eps_i`` with ``eps_i`` uniform on
    ``[rate_lo, rate_hi]``; ``n_targets`` wrong classes drawn at random carry
    a share ``conc`` of the noise mass, split by a Dirichlet(``alpha``); the
    rest is spread uniformly over the remaining classes.  ``eps_i`` is capped
    so that the diagonal stays strictly the largest entry of its row (without
    it a row whose mass sits on one target would make the row's identity
    ambiguous, and the estimand ill-posed).
    """
    k = max(1, min(int(p["n_targets"]), C - 1))
    conc, alpha = float(p["conc"]), float(p["alpha"])
    T = np.zeros((C, C))
    for i in range(C):
        others = np.array([j for j in range(C) if j != i])
        tgt = rng.choice(others, size=k, replace=False)
        row = np.zeros(C)
        row[tgt] = conc * rng.dirichlet(np.full(k, alpha))
        rest = np.setdiff1d(others, tgt)
        if len(rest) and conc < 1.0:
            row[rest] = (1.0 - conc) / len(rest)
        row /= row.sum()
        eps = float(rng.uniform(p["rate_lo"], p["rate_hi"]))
        eps = min(eps, 0.9 / (1.0 + float(row.max())))
        T[i] = eps * row
        T[i, i] = 1.0 - eps
    return T


def _draw(spec, rng, data):
    """One salted view: the rows and noisy labels the client sees, and the private truth."""
    p = lab.resolve(spec, rng)
    n_all = int(p["n_train"]) + int(p["n_test"])
    idx = np.sort(lab.subsample(rng, len(data["feats"]), n_all))
    X = np.asarray(data["feats"][idx], np.float64)
    y = np.asarray(data["labels"][idx], np.int64)
    order = rng.permutation(len(X))
    X, y = X[order], y[order]

    mu, sd = X.mean(0), X.std(0)
    sd[sd == 0] = 1.0
    Z = ((X - mu) / sd) @ lab.haar_rotation(rng, X.shape[1])[:, :int(p["dim"])]
    scale = float(np.mean(Z.std(0)))
    Zn = Z + float(p["noise"]) * scale * rng.standard_normal(Z.shape)

    ntr = int(p["n_train"])
    T = _draw_transition(rng, _C, p)
    cum = T.cumsum(1)
    u = rng.random(ntr)
    y_noisy = (u[:, None] > cum[y[:ntr]]).sum(1).astype(np.int64)
    y_noisy = np.clip(y_noisy, 0, _C - 1)

    priv = {"T": T, "y_tr": y[:ntr], "y_te": y[ntr:], "Ztr": Zn[:ntr], "Zte": Zn[ntr:],
            "clean_tr": Z[:ntr], "clean_te": Z[ntr:], "scale": scale, "noise": float(p["noise"]),
            "y_noisy": y_noisy}
    view = {"features": Zn[:ntr].astype(np.float32), "noisy_labels": y_noisy, "n_classes": _C}
    return view, priv


def _empirical_T(y_clean, y_noisy, C):
    """The transition matrix realised by this sample (the in-sample floor of any estimator)."""
    T = np.zeros((C, C))
    for i in range(C):
        m = y_clean == i
        if m.sum():
            T[i] = np.bincount(y_noisy[m], minlength=C) / m.sum()
        else:
            T[i, i] = 1.0
    return T


def _project(T):
    """Row-stochastic projection of a submitted matrix (documented in the task description)."""
    T = np.clip(np.asarray(T, np.float64), 0.0, None)
    s = T.sum(1, keepdims=True)
    out = np.where(s > 0, T / np.where(s > 0, s, 1.0), 1.0 / T.shape[1])
    return out


def serve(spec, seed, rng, sess):
    data = {"feats": lab.load_array(f"features/{spec['pool']}_feats.npy"),
            "labels": lab.load_array(f"features/{spec['pool']}_labels.npy")}
    errs, accs, floors, curve = [], [], [], {}
    for rep in range(int(spec["reps"])):
        view, priv = _draw(spec, rng, data)
        n = len(priv["y_noisy"])

        def expect(msg):
            try:
                return lab.check_array(msg.get("transition"), (_C, _C), name="transition")
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise lab.ProtocolError(f"result: {exc}") from None

        T_hat = _project(sess.query({}, expect, rep=rep, **view))
        errs.append(float(np.abs(T_hat - priv["T"]).sum() / _C))
        floors.append(float(np.abs(_empirical_T(priv["y_tr"], priv["y_noisy"], _C)
                                   - priv["T"]).sum() / _C))
        Xtr, Xte = _design(priv["Ztr"]), _design(priv["Zte"])
        W = _fit_forward(Xtr, priv["y_noisy"], T_hat)
        accs.append(lab.accuracy(priv["y_te"], np.argmax(Xte @ W, 1)))
        if rep == 0:
            # Difficulty diagnostics, once per run: how well a head fitted on
            # CLEAN labels separates the classes on this view, at the
            # setting's noise level and at half and twice that level.  They
            # calibrate the regime; they are not scored.
            for tag, mult in (("x06", 0.6), ("x08", 0.8), ("x10", 1.0), ("x14", 1.4)):
                s = priv["noise"] * mult * priv["scale"]
                tr = _design(priv["clean_tr"] + s * rng.standard_normal(priv["clean_tr"].shape))
                te = _design(priv["clean_te"] + s * rng.standard_normal(priv["clean_te"].shape))
                curve[f"probe_acc_{tag}"] = _probe_acc(tr, priv["y_tr"], te, priv["y_te"], _C)
    return {"t_estimation_error": float(np.mean(errs)),
            "forward_corrected_test_acc": float(np.mean(accs)),
            "t_error_sd": float(np.std(errs)),
            "empirical_floor": float(np.mean(floors)),
            "n_reps": float(len(errs)), **curve}

"""ml-ood-score-design: an OOD scoring function on a frozen CIFAR-10 classifier.

Protocol (one round per draw): the server sends ``query`` with the fitting
material a post-hoc detector may use -- a salted subsample of the frozen
network's in-distribution TRAINING features (``train_feats``, ``(n_train,
512)``), their logits, their class labels, and the classifier head
(``fc_weight`` ``(10, 512)``, ``fc_bias`` ``(10,)``) -- together with the
rows to score, ``feats`` ``(n, 512)`` and ``logits`` ``(n, 10)``: a shuffled
mixture of held-out CIFAR-10 test images and OOD images, in unknown
proportion, with no source marker.  The client answers ``result`` with
``scores`` ``(n,)``, HIGHER = MORE OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION.  The server scores
AUROC with the OOD rows as the positive class; the membership never leaves
this process.

Frozen network: ResNet-18 trained on CIFAR-10 (``build_data.py``), features
= the 512-d post-average-pool activations, ``logits = feats @ fc_weight.T +
fc_bias``.  Every draw is a SALTED VIEW of the baked features (the
public-data leak rule of ``mlvision_lab``): a Haar-random orthogonal change
of basis ``Q`` is applied to the feature space and to the head (``feats @
Q``, ``fc_weight @ Q``), isotropic Gaussian noise of a few per cent of the
feature scale is added, and the logits are recomputed from the noisy
rotated features so the interface invariant holds exactly.  Distances,
inner products, norms, class-conditional Gaussians, principal subspaces and
the logits are preserved; the coordinate axes are not the network's units
(unit-wise activation statistics are deliberately not part of this
interface).

What the salted view does NOT do: hide which stored row a scored row is.
The logits are preserved by construction, so the logits sent are the stored
``<set>_logits.npy`` rows plus noise of order ``sigma * ||w_c||``
(``(X@Q + E) @ (W@Q).T = X@W.T + E@Q.T@W.T``), and a client that could read
the stored pools would recover the membership of every scored row with one
10-d nearest-neighbour lookup (no noise level prevents it without also
destroying the honest signal).  That is why the pools are NOT readable:
every array under ``/opt/mlvision-lab-data`` is encrypted at image build
(``build_data.py``), the key exists at run time only in the task's
per-setting script -- present at verification time, never during the
agent's phase -- and the guard hands it to this evaluator process alone
while the client runs as an unprivileged uid that cannot read the
evaluator's environment or memory, the script directory, or the blobs
(mode 0600 root).  ``lab.load_array`` decrypts into memory.  The salting is
what keeps the INTERFACE honest (no unit axes to exploit); the encryption
and the uid switch are what keep the data private.

A parameter given as a two-element list ``[lo, hi]`` is a RANGE: every draw
samples its own value with the salted rng (integers inclusive, floats
uniform), including the shares of the OOD sources in ``ood`` (normalised to
sum to one after sampling).  The hidden setting is specified this way so
that reading this module does not pin down a distribution to tune to.
"""
import numpy as np

import mlvision_lab as lab

CUSTOM = "custom_ood_score.py"
# Seconds per setting for the client (the server enforces the same deadline).
# Measured through the rendered bundle (8 vCPU per container, the
# nine setting x seed cells of a baseline running concurrently, one thread
# per process): a cell -- eight draws, server and client together -- takes
# 10-15 s for a fit-free score, 23-33 s for brute-force k-NN and 32-36 s for
# ViM on a normal host, and up to 116 s on a slow one (ViM, the worst cell
# seen).  400 s is > 3x that worst cell and ~11x a typical one, leaving room
# for heavier estimators (per-class covariances, larger neighbour sets).
BUDGET = 400

_TRAIN, _ID_TEST, _DIM, _N_CLASSES = "cifar10_train", "cifar10_test", 512, 10

ENVS = {
    # ood: source -> share of the OOD rows (a dict; shares may be ranges);
    # n_train: ID training rows sent for fitting (of 50000); n_id / n_ood:
    # held-out ID test rows / OOD rows scored per draw; noise: relative sd of
    # the isotropic noise added after the rotation; reps: independent draws
    # averaged (each with its own rotation, subsamples and noise).
    "far-svhn": {"ood": {"svhn_test": 1.0}, "n_train": 20000, "n_id": 2000, "n_ood": 2000,
                 "noise": 0.05, "reps": 8},
    "near-cifar100": {"ood": {"cifar100_test": 1.0}, "n_train": 20000, "n_id": 2000, "n_ood": 2000,
                      "noise": 0.05, "reps": 8},
    # Hidden: a mixture of OOD sources not used by the visible settings --
    # mostly a near-OOD natural-image set with a far-OOD texture set and a
    # far-OOD digit set -- with the shares, the fitting-set size, the scored
    # counts and the noise level all drawn from ranges.
    "mixed-ood": {"ood": {"tin_val": [0.5, 0.8], "dtd": [0.1, 0.3], "mnist_test": [0.05, 0.2]},
                  "n_train": [12000, 20000], "n_id": [1500, 2500], "n_ood": [1500, 2500],
                  "noise": [0.03, 0.08], "reps": 8},
}


def _sources(spec):
    return sorted(spec["ood"])


def _draw(spec, rng, data):
    """One salted view: fitting material, rows to score, and the private membership."""
    p = lab.resolve(spec, rng)
    shares = lab.resolve(spec["ood"], rng)
    total = float(sum(shares.values()))
    shares = {k: float(v) / total for k, v in shares.items()}
    Q = lab.haar_rotation(rng, _DIM)

    tr_idx = lab.subsample(rng, len(data["train_feats"]), p["n_train"])
    train = np.asarray(data["train_feats"][np.sort(tr_idx)], np.float64) @ Q
    sigma = float(p["noise"]) * float(np.mean(train.std(0)))
    train += sigma * rng.standard_normal(train.shape)
    labels = np.asarray(data["train_labels"][np.sort(tr_idx)], np.int64)

    id_idx = lab.subsample(rng, len(data["id_feats"]), p["n_id"])
    blocks = [np.asarray(data["id_feats"][np.sort(id_idx)], np.float64)]
    is_ood = [np.zeros(len(id_idx), bool)]
    names = _sources(spec)
    counts = [int(round(shares[k] * p["n_ood"])) for k in names]
    for name, cnt in zip(names, counts):
        if cnt <= 0:
            continue
        pool = data["ood"][name]
        idx = lab.subsample(rng, len(pool), cnt)
        blocks.append(np.asarray(pool[np.sort(idx)], np.float64))
        is_ood.append(np.ones(len(idx), bool))
    X = np.concatenate(blocks) @ Q
    X += sigma * rng.standard_normal(X.shape)
    is_ood = np.concatenate(is_ood)
    perm = rng.permutation(len(X))
    X, is_ood = X[perm], is_ood[perm]

    W = data["fc_weight"] @ Q                       # (10, 512): logits = feats @ W.T + b
    b = data["fc_bias"]
    view = {
        "train_feats": train.astype(np.float32), "train_logits": (train @ W.T + b).astype(np.float32),
        "train_labels": labels, "fc_weight": W.astype(np.float32), "fc_bias": b.astype(np.float32),
        "feats": X.astype(np.float32), "logits": (X @ W.T + b).astype(np.float32),
    }
    return view, is_ood


def serve(spec, seed, rng, sess):
    # Decrypted into this process's memory (a few hundred MB, well under a
    # second); nothing is written back to disk.
    data = {
        "train_feats": lab.load_array(f"features/{_TRAIN}_feats.npy"),
        "train_labels": lab.load_array(f"features/{_TRAIN}_labels.npy"),
        "id_feats": lab.load_array(f"features/{_ID_TEST}_feats.npy"),
        "fc_weight": np.asarray(lab.load_array("features/fc_weight.npy"), np.float64),
        "fc_bias": np.asarray(lab.load_array("features/fc_bias.npy"), np.float64),
        "ood": {name: lab.load_array(f"features/{name}_feats.npy") for name in _sources(spec)},
    }
    aurocs, fprs = [], []
    for rep in range(int(spec["reps"])):
        view, is_ood = _draw(spec, rng, data)
        n = len(is_ood)

        def expect(msg, n=n):
            try:
                return lab.check_array(msg.get("scores"), (n,), name="scores")
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise lab.ProtocolError(f"result: {exc}") from None

        scores = sess.query({}, expect, rep=rep, **view)
        aurocs.append(lab.auroc(scores[is_ood], scores[~is_ood]))
        # FPR at 95 % TPR on the ID side: the fraction of OOD rows accepted as
        # ID when the threshold keeps 95 % of the ID rows ("higher = more OOD"
        # scores, so negate for the helper's "higher = more ID" convention).
        fprs.append(lab.fpr_at_tpr(-scores[~is_ood], -scores[is_ood], 0.95))
    return {"auroc": float(np.mean(aurocs)), "fpr95": float(np.mean(fprs)),
            "auroc_sd": float(np.std(aurocs)), "n_reps": float(len(aurocs))}

"""ml-pu-learning-risk: the training objective of positive-unlabeled learning.

Protocol (ONE round per setting run): the server sends ``query`` with the
material a PU learner is allowed to see, in the censoring protocol of the
reference papers (Kiryo et al. 2017, sec. 5; Zhao et al. 2022, Table 1):

* ``x_u`` -- the WHOLE training split of the setting's image dataset, as
  raw ``uint8`` images ``(n_u, H, W, C)``, every row unlabelled, in a salted
  random order (a uniform sample of the marginal, so its positive rate is
  the class prior);
* ``x_p`` -- ``n_l`` LABELLED POSITIVES drawn uniformly (salted) from the
  positive rows of the same training split; as in both reference
  implementations they are *also* present, unlabelled, in ``x_u``;
* ``prior`` -- the class prior pi = p(y = +1), the positive fraction of the
  training split (both papers assume pi known);
* ``arch`` / ``norm`` -- which of the two fixed networks of the papers the
  driver trains (``mlp``: the 6-layer d-300-300-300-300-1 batch-normalised
  MLP; ``cnn``: the 13-layer all-convolutional net) and the fixed input
  normalisation.

The client trains the FIXED network with the editable objective and answers
``result`` with ``state`` -- the trained network's ``state_dict`` as plain
float arrays -- and ``threshold``, a finite float: the decision rule is
``logit >= threshold``.  The client never sees a test image.  THIS process
rebuilds the network from its own class definitions below (it never imports
anything from the workspace), loads the arrays with ``strict`` key and shape
checks -- so a submission cannot enlarge or change the network -- runs it on
the held-out test split, and scores.  The test images and every label live
only in this process's memory.

Metrics (the reference papers'): ``test_error`` (the zero-one error of
Kiryo et al.; 1 - ACC of Zhao et al.) is scored; ``precision``, ``recall``,
``f1``, ``auc`` and ``ap`` (Zhao et al., Table 2; AUC and AP are computed
from the logits and do not depend on the threshold) and ``pred_pos_rate``
are reported alongside.

The pools are the image's ENCRYPTED arrays (``build_data.py``); the key
reaches this process only (``mlvision_guard.sh``), the client runs as an
unprivileged uid, and the rendered task has no network in any phase.  There
is no synthetic generator on purpose: a synthetic PU problem is cloneable
(the client could draw its own labelled sample from the disclosed generator).
"""
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

import mlvision_lab as lab

CUSTOM = "pu_driver.py"
# The client entry is the fixed driver (it enforces the protocol); its digest is pinned.
TRUSTED_CLIENT = "pu_driver.py"
# Seconds per setting run for the client (the server enforces the same
# deadline): data transfer, 120 training epochs of the fixed network, the
# state transfer.  Sized at >= 3x the slowest baseline's measured elapsed
# (measured: dist_pu on the CNN setting).
BUDGET = 12000

# train / test: the image pools; pos: the underlying class ids that form the
# positive class; n_l: labelled positives; arch / norm: the fixed network and
# input normalisation of the reference papers for that dataset.
ENVS = {
    # Kiryo et al. 2017, Table 2 / sec. 5 and nnPUlearning --preset exp-mnist:
    # even digits positive (pi = 0.49), n_p = 1000, U = the 60k training set,
    # 6-layer MLP on raw pixels.
    "mnist-evenodd": {"train": "mnist_train", "test": "mnist_test", "pos": [0, 2, 4, 6, 8],
                      "n_l": 1000, "arch": "mlp", "norm": "unit"},
    # Zhao et al. 2022, Table 1: Fashion-MNIST, "top" classes 0/2/4/6 positive
    # (pi = 0.4), U = the 60k training set, 6-layer MLP -- with n_L = 250, a
    # smaller labelled set than Dist-PU's 500 (at 500 the best PU method already
    # closed ~80 % of the gap to supervised training, measured).
    "fmnist-top": {"train": "fmnist_train", "test": "fmnist_test", "pos": [0, 2, 4, 6],
                   "n_l": 250, "arch": "mlp", "norm": "unit"},
    # Kiryo et al. 2017, Table 2 and Zhao et al. 2022, Table 1: CIFAR-10,
    # vehicles (airplane, automobile, ship, truck) positive (pi = 0.4),
    # n_L = 1000, U = the 50k training set, the 13-layer all-conv CNN.
    "cifar10-vehicle": {"train": "cifar10_train", "test": "cifar10_test", "pos": [0, 1, 8, 9],
                        "n_l": 1000, "arch": "cnn", "norm": "imagenet"},
}

_IMAGENET_MEAN = (0.485, 0.456, 0.406)
_IMAGENET_STD = (0.229, 0.224, 0.225)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# them, this process evaluates them).  Ray-rui/Dist-PU models/modelForFMNIST.py
# and models/modelForCIFAR10.py == kiryor/nnPUlearning model.py
# MultiLayerPerceptron / CNN.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class MLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.l1 = nn.Linear(dim, 300, bias=False)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm1d(300)
        self.l2 = nn.Linear(300, 300, bias=False)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm1d(300)
        self.l3 = nn.Linear(300, 300, bias=False)
        self.bn3 = nn.BatchNorm1d(300)
        self.l4 = nn.Linear(300, 300, bias=False)
        self.bn4 = nn.BatchNorm1d(300)

    def forward(self, x):

        x = F.relu(self.bn2(self.l2(x)))
        x = F.relu(self.bn3(self.l3(x)))
        x = F.relu(self.bn4(self.l4(x)))
        return self.l5(x).reshape(-1)


class CNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):

        self.conv3 = nn.Conv2d(96, 96, kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1)
        self.bn3 = nn.BatchNorm2d(96)
        self.conv4 = nn.Conv2d(96, 192, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.bn4 = nn.BatchNorm2d(192)
        self.conv5 = nn.Conv2d(192, 192, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.bn5 = nn.BatchNorm2d(192)
        self.conv6 = nn.Conv2d(192, 192, kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1)
        self.bn6 = nn.BatchNorm2d(192)
        self.conv7 = nn.Conv2d(192, 192, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.bn7 = nn.BatchNorm2d(192)
        self.conv8 = nn.Conv2d(192, 192, kernel_size=1)
        self.bn8 = nn.BatchNorm2d(192)

        x = F.relu(self.l2(x))

def _net(arch, shape):
    if arch == "mlp":
        return MLP(int(np.prod(shape[1:])))
    if arch == "cnn":
        return CNN()
    raise ValueError(arch)


def _normalise(x_uint8, norm, device):
    """(n, H, W, C) uint8 -> the float tensor the network sees (the driver does the same)."""
    x = torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(x_uint8)).to(device).permute(0, 3, 1, 2).float() / 255.0
    if norm == "imagenet":
        mean = torch.tensor(_IMAGENET_MEAN, device=device).view(1, 3, 1, 1)
        std = torch.tensor(_IMAGENET_STD, device=device).view(1, 3, 1, 1)
        x = (x - mean) / std
    elif norm != "unit":
        raise ValueError(norm)
    return x


def _load_state(net, state):
    """Strict load of client arrays: exactly the network's keys, shapes and dtypes."""
    if not isinstance(state, dict):
        raise lab.ProtocolError("result: state must be a dict of arrays")
    ref = net.state_dict()
    if set(state) != set(ref):
        missing, extra = sorted(set(ref) - set(state)), sorted(set(state) - set(ref))
        raise lab.ProtocolError(f"result: state keys differ from the fixed network "
                                f"(missing {missing[:3]}, unexpected {extra[:3]})")
    new = {}
    for k, t in ref.items():
        a = np.asarray(state[k])
        if t.dim() == 0 and a.shape == (1,):
            a = a.reshape(())             # the wire format sends 0-d arrays as (1,)
        if a.dtype == object or tuple(a.shape) != tuple(t.shape):
            raise lab.ProtocolError(f"result: state[{k!r}] must have shape {tuple(t.shape)}, got {a.shape}")
        if t.dtype == torch.long:
            if not np.issubdtype(a.dtype, np.integer):
                raise lab.ProtocolError(f"result: state[{k!r}] must be integer")
            new[k] = torch.from_numpy(a.astype(np.int64))
        else:
            if not np.issubdtype(a.dtype, np.floating):
                raise lab.ProtocolError(f"result: state[{k!r}] must be floating point")
            new[k] = torch.from_numpy(a.astype(np.float32))
    net.load_state_dict(new, strict=True)
    return net


def _metrics(logits, y, threshold):
    from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, roc_auc_score
    # A diverged network (non-finite weights) is a bad result, not a crash:
    # its non-finite logits score as 0 (ties everywhere, AUC 0.5) and are
    # predicted negative.
    finite = np.isfinite(logits)
    s = np.where(finite, logits, 0.0)
    pred = (finite & (logits >= threshold)).astype(np.int64)
    tp = float(np.sum((pred == 1) & (y == 1)))
    fp = float(np.sum((pred == 1) & (y == 0)))
    fn = float(np.sum((pred == 0) & (y == 1)))
    prec = tp / (tp + fp + 1e-8)
    rec = tp / (tp + fn + 1e-8)
    return {
        "test_error": float(np.mean(pred != y)),
        "precision": prec, "recall": rec, "f1": 2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec + 1e-8),
        "auc": float(roc_auc_score(y, s)), "ap": float(average_precision_score(y, s)),
        "pred_pos_rate": float(np.mean(pred)), "nonfinite_rate": float(1.0 - np.mean(finite)),
    }


def _draw_rng(seed, spec):
    """The draw's generator: a function of the harness seed and the evaluator's secret key.

    The lab core hands every server an ``os.urandom``-salted rng; this task instead derives
    its draw (which positives are labelled, the order of U) from the seed AND a digest of the
    data key, which exists only in this process.  So a (setting, seed) cell is reproducible
    run to run -- the anchors are paired across arms -- while nothing in the workspace or the
    client can regenerate the draw.
    """
    import hashlib
    salt = hashlib.sha256(b"ml-pu-learning-risk draw\n" + lab.data_key() + spec["train"].encode()).digest()
    return np.random.default_rng([int(seed), int.from_bytes(salt[:8], "little")])


def serve(spec, seed, rng, sess):
    rng = _draw_rng(seed, spec)
    pos = list(int(c) for c in spec["pos"])
    x_tr = lab.load_array(f"arrays/{spec['train']}_x.npy")
    y_tr = np.isin(lab.load_array(f"arrays/{spec['train']}_y.npy"), pos)
    x_te = lab.load_array(f"arrays/{spec['test']}_x.npy")
    y_te = np.isin(lab.load_array(f"arrays/{spec['test']}_y.npy"), pos).astype(np.int64)
    prior = float(np.mean(y_tr))

    # U = the whole training split in a salted order (the stored pools are
    # sorted by class for some datasets, so the order must carry nothing);
    # P = n_l positives drawn uniformly from it (censoring protocol).
    perm = rng.permutation(len(x_tr))
    p_idx = rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(y_tr), size=int(spec["n_l"]), replace=False)
    view = {"x_p": np.ascontiguousarray(x_tr[p_idx]), "x_u": np.ascontiguousarray(x_tr[perm]),
            "prior": prior, "arch": spec["arch"], "norm": spec["norm"]}
    del perm, p_idx, y_tr

    def expect(msg):
        thr = msg.get("threshold")
        if isinstance(thr, bool) or not isinstance(thr, (int, float)) or not np.isfinite(thr):
            raise lab.ProtocolError("result: threshold must be a finite number")
        net = _load_state(_net(spec["arch"], x_te.shape), msg.get("state"))
        return net, float(thr)

    net, thr = sess.query({}, expect, rep=0, **view)
    del view
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    net = net.to(device).eval()
    logits = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i in range(0, len(x_te), 500):
            logits.append(net(_normalise(x_te[i:i + 500], spec["norm"], device)).double().cpu().numpy())
    out = _metrics(np.concatenate(logits), y_te, thr)
    out.update({"prior": prior, "threshold": thr})
    return out

# Positive-unlabeled learning: the training objective (the fixed driver is pu_driver.py).
import math
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


# =====================================================================
# EDITABLE: PUObjective
# =====================================================================
class PUObjective:
    """The training objective of a positive-unlabeled classifier.

    The driver (``pu_driver.py``, read-only) builds the fixed network, owns the
    optimiser, the learning-rate schedule, the number of epochs and the
    minibatches, and calls the three methods below.

    ``begin(x, labeled, prior)`` is called once before training with the whole
    PU training set: ``x`` ``(N, C, H, W)`` float tensor on the training
    device (the unlabelled rows followed by the labelled positives, already
    normalised), ``labeled`` ``(N,)`` bool (True = a labelled positive;
    False = an unlabelled row, a ``prior`` fraction of which are positive)
    and the class prior ``prior`` = p(y = +1).  Row ``i`` of ``x`` is the row
    that ``idx == i`` refers to in ``loss``.

    ``loss(model, x, labeled, idx, prior, epoch, n_epochs)`` is called once per
    optimisation step with the network (in train mode; call it yourself),
    a minibatch ``x`` of the PU training set, its ``labeled`` mask, the row
    indices ``idx`` of the minibatch in the set passed to ``begin``, the
    prior, the 0-based ``epoch`` and the run length ``n_epochs``.  It must
    return a scalar tensor with a gradient; the driver backpropagates it and
    takes the optimiser step.  It may feed the network anything (the batch,
    mixed or perturbed inputs, the stored set), keep state on ``self``, and
    switch the network between train and eval mode; it may NOT change the
    network's parameters or its structure, call ``backward`` itself, or
    touch the optimiser (the driver checks and invalidates the run).

    ``threshold(model, x, labeled, prior)`` is called once after training
    (on a copy of the network, eval mode, no_grad) and returns the decision
    threshold on the network's output: a test row is labelled positive
    when ``model(row) >= threshold``.

    Rules of the editable file (enforced by the driver before import): only
    ``math``, ``numpy``, ``torch``, ``torch.nn`` and ``torch.nn.functional``
    may be imported, only this class may be defined, and attributes may be
    assigned on ``self`` only.
    """

    def __init__(self, seed: int = 0):
        self.seed = int(seed)

    def begin(self, x, labeled, prior):
        pass

    def loss(self, model, x, labeled, idx, prior, epoch, n_epochs):
        # Unbiased PU risk (du Plessis et al. 2015) with the sigmoid loss
        # l(z) = sigmoid(-z):  pi * E_p[l(g)] + (E_u[l(-g)] - pi * E_p[l(-g)]).
        g = model(x)
        pos = labeled.float()
        unl = 1.0 - pos
        n_p = torch.clamp(pos.sum(), min=1.0)
        n_u = torch.clamp(unl.sum(), min=1.0)
        positive_risk = torch.sum(prior * pos / n_p * torch.sigmoid(-g))
        negative_risk = torch.sum((unl / n_u - prior * pos / n_p) * torch.sigmoid(g))
        return positive_risk + negative_risk

    def threshold(self, model, x, labeled, prior):
        return 0.0

OPS = [{"op": "replace", "file": _FILE, "start_line": 11, "end_line": 68, "content": '''class PUObjective:
    """Dist-PU (Zhao, Xu, Jiang, Wen & Huang, "Dist-PU: Positive-Unlabeled
    Learning From a Label Distribution Perspective", CVPR 2022).

    Port of Ray-rui/Dist-PU (commit cb74be1a):
      * warm-up (the first half of the run, train.py ``warm_up`` with
        ``create_loss(args)`` at ``--entropy 1``, losses/factory.py 18-22):
        LabelDistributionLoss(g, y) + co_mu * H(sigmoid(clamp(g, -10, 10))
        on the unlabelled rows), co_mu = 2e-3;
      * Dist-PU phase (the second half, train.py ``set_up_for_dist_pu`` /
        ``train_mixup`` lines 152-185 / ``update_co_entropy``): pseudo-labels
        of every row are initialised by one eval-mode pass over the PU set
        (dataTools/mixupDataset.py), labelled rows are forced to 1, the batch
        is mixed with lam ~ Beta(alpha, alpha), alpha = 6 (customized/mixup.py
        ``mixup_two_targets``), and the loss is
            LabelDistributionLoss(clamp(g)) + co_entropy(e) * H(s[unlabelled])
            + 0.04 * H(s_mix) + 5.0 * mixup_bce(s_mix, y_a, y_b, lam),
        co_entropy(e) = (1 - cos(e / 60 * pi / 2)) * 0.004 at the phase's
        epoch e; the stored pseudo-labels of the batch rows are then replaced
        by the batch's detached scores;
      * LabelDistributionLoss (losses/distributionLoss.py) with num_bins = 1,
        the polar proxy and L1: the triangular-kernel histogram of the scores
        of the labelled rows against [0, 1] and of the unlabelled rows
        against [1 - pi, pi], the latter weighted 1 / (2 pi).
    The two phases' optimisers (Adam 5e-4 / 5e-3 then 5e-5 / 1e-3, cosine)
    are the task's shared driver.  Decision rule: sigmoid(g) >= 0.5, i.e.
    g >= 0 (utils.py ``validate``).
    """

    CO_MU = 2e-3
    CO_ENTROPY = 4e-3
    CO_MIX_ENTROPY = 4e-2
    CO_MIXUP = 5.0
    ALPHA = 6.0
    NUM_BINS = 1

    def __init__(self, seed: int = 0):
        self.seed = int(seed)
        self.rng = np.random.RandomState(self.seed)
        self.psudo = None

    def begin(self, x, labeled, prior):
        self.x_all = x
        self.labeled_all = labeled
        step = 1.0 / self.NUM_BINS
        self.step = step
        self.t = torch.arange(0, 1 + step, step, device=x.device).view(1, -1)
        proxy_p = torch.zeros(self.NUM_BINS + 1, device=x.device)
        proxy_p[-1] = 1.0
        proxy_n = torch.zeros(self.NUM_BINS + 1, device=x.device)
        proxy_n[0] = 1.0
        self.proxy_p = proxy_p
        self.proxy_mix = prior * proxy_p + (1 - prior) * proxy_n
        self.frac_prior = 1.0 / (2 * prior)

    def histogram(self, scores):
        hist = torch.abs(scores.view(-1, 1).repeat(1, self.t.shape[1]) - self.t)
        inds = hist > self.step
        hist = self.step - hist
        hist = hist.masked_fill(inds, 0.0)
        return hist.sum(dim=0) / (len(scores) * self.step)

    def dist_loss(self, outputs, labeled):
        scores = torch.sigmoid(outputs)
        s_p = scores[labeled]
        s_u = scores[~labeled]
        l_p = 0.0
        l_u = 0.0
        if s_p.numel() > 0:
            l_p = F.l1_loss(self.histogram(s_p), self.proxy_p, reduction="mean")
        if s_u.numel() > 0:
            l_u = F.l1_loss(self.histogram(s_u), self.proxy_mix, reduction="mean")
        return l_p + self.frac_prior * l_u

    @staticmethod
    def entropy(scores):
        return -torch.mean(scores * torch.log(scores) + (1 - scores) * torch.log(1 - scores))

    @staticmethod
    def mixup_bce(scores, targets_a, targets_b, lam):
        return lam * F.binary_cross_entropy(scores, targets_a) \\
            + (1 - lam) * F.binary_cross_entropy(scores, targets_b)

    def loss(self, model, x, labeled, idx, prior, epoch, n_epochs):
        warm = n_epochs // 2
        if epoch < warm:
            outputs = model(x)
            scores = torch.sigmoid(torch.clamp(outputs, min=-10, max=10))
            return self.dist_loss(outputs, labeled) + self.CO_MU * self.entropy(scores[~labeled])
        if self.psudo is None:
            model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                self.psudo = torch.cat([torch.sigmoid(model(self.x_all[i:i + 128]))
                                        for i in range(0, len(self.x_all), 128)])
            model.train()
        e = epoch - warm
        co_entropy = (1 - math.cos((float(e) / (n_epochs - warm)) * (math.pi / 2))) * self.CO_ENTROPY
        psudos = self.psudo[idx].clone()
        psudos[labeled] = 1.0
        lam = self.rng.beta(self.ALPHA, self.ALPHA) if self.ALPHA > 0 else 1.0
        perm = torch.randperm(x.shape[0], device=x.device)
        mixed_x = lam * x + (1 - lam) * x[perm]
        y_a, y_b = psudos, psudos[perm]

                 + co_entropy * self.entropy(scores_[~labeled])
                 + self.CO_MIX_ENTROPY * self.entropy(scores)

    def threshold(self, model, x, labeled, prior):
        return 0.0

"""Fixed driver of ml-pu-learning-risk (READ-ONLY): trains the fixed network with the editable objective.

The guard runs THIS file as the untrusted client.  It receives the PU sample
from the private evaluator, trains the setting's fixed network with
``PUObjective`` from ``custom_pu.py`` under the fixed protocol below, and
sends back the trained weights and the decision threshold.  It never sees a
test image or a label: the evaluator rebuilds the network from its own class
definitions, loads the weights with strict key/shape checks, and scores them
on the held-out test split in its own process.

Training protocol (the experimental control; Zhao et al. 2022, sec. 4.1 and
Ray-rui/Dist-PU train.py):
  * the PU training set is the unlabelled rows followed by the labelled
    positives.  Minibatches of ``BATCH`` rows are STRATIFIED: each holds
    k_p = max(ceil(BATCH * n_L / N), K_MIN_POS) labelled positives, drawn by
    cycling through a reshuffled permutation of the labelled set, and
    BATCH - k_p unlabelled rows; an epoch covers the unlabelled set once in a
    fresh order (the last minibatch smaller).  A uniformly shuffled slice (the
    reference DataLoader) starves the risk estimators when n_L / N is small --
    at 250 labelled positives among 60,250 rows a batch of 256 holds 1.06 on
    average and 35 % hold none, and nnPU collapsed to the all-negative
    classifier -- whereas Kiryo et al. ran their n_p = 100 regime with ~50
    positives per batch (stratified minibatches);
  * epochs [0, EPOCHS_1): Adam(lr 5e-4, weight decay 5e-3), learning rate
    cosine-annealed per epoch with T_max = EPOCHS_2;
  * epochs [EPOCHS_1, EPOCHS_1 + EPOCHS_2): a fresh Adam(lr 5e-5, weight
    decay 1e-3), cosine-annealed per epoch with T_max = EPOCHS_2 and
    eta_min = 0.7 * 5e-5;
  * the final network is the one returned (no model selection).

Integrity checks (a failure makes the run INVALID): the editable module is
parsed against an allowlist (see _check_source); the objective receives a
``Network`` handle (call / train / eval), never the module; every operator the
objective's calls execute is charged by a work-counting dispatch mode (see
WORK_CAP); no operator override or dispatch mode may be installed; the
parameters change only through the driver's optimiser step, whose
hyper-parameters are checked every step; batch-norm statistics are recomputed
by the driver; ``threshold`` runs on a copy of the network.
"""
import argparse
import types as _types
import ast
import copy
import math
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils._python_dispatch import TorchDispatchMode
from torch.utils._pytree import tree_leaves
from torch.utils.flop_counter import flop_registry

from mlvision_lab import run_client

BATCH = 256
K_MIN_POS = 4          # at least this many labelled positives in every minibatch
EPOCHS_1 = 60
EPOCHS_2 = 60
LR_1, WD_1 = 5e-4, 5e-3
LR_2, WD_2 = 5e-5, 1e-3

# Compute charge.  Every call into the objective (begin, loss + the driver's backward of its
# loss, threshold) runs under a work-counting dispatch mode (_WorkCounter): every aten operator
# it executes -- through the network or not, forward or backward, on any device -- is charged
# its FLOPs if torch's flop registry knows it (mm / addmm / bmm / conv / conv backward / sdpa
# ...), otherwise the larger of its input and output element counts (views are free).  The unit
# is the counted work of one plain forward+backward pass of the fixed network on a minibatch of
# BATCH rows, measured the same way before any objective code exists.  The total may be at most
# WORK_CAP units per optimisation step plus WORK_ALLOWANCE full forward+backward passes over the
# PU training set (e.g. a pseudo-label or threshold pass).  Dist-PU, the costliest published

WORK_ALLOWANCE = 1.0

_ALLOWED_MODULES = {"math", "numpy", "numpy.random", "torch", "torch.nn",

def _allowed_leaf(obj):
    """What a module-rooted attribute chain may resolve to: functions, a few classes, constants."""
    import types
    if isinstance(obj, (bool, int, float, complex, str, torch.dtype)):
        return True
    if isinstance(obj, (types.FunctionType, types.BuiltinFunctionType, types.MethodType,
                        np.ufunc)) or type(obj).__name__ in ("builtin_function_or_method",
                                                             "_VariableFunctionsClass"):
        return True
    if isinstance(obj, type):
        if obj in (torch.no_grad, torch.enable_grad, torch.inference_mode, torch.Generator,
                   np.random.RandomState, np.random.Generator):
            return True
        if issubclass(obj, np.generic):
            return True
        try:
            import torch.distributions as _dist
            if issubclass(obj, _dist.Distribution):
                return True
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            pass
    return False


def _check_source(src):
    """AST guard of the editable module (see the module docstring)."""
    import importlib
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    aliases = {}                                              # local name -> module dotted path
    classes = [n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef)]
    for node in tree.body:
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            for a in node.names:
                if a.name not in _ALLOWED_IMPORTS:
                    raise ObjectiveRejected(f"import of {a.name!r} is not allowed")
                if a.asname:
                    aliases[a.asname] = a.name
                else:
                    aliases[a.name.split(".")[0]] = a.name.split(".")[0]
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            if node.module not in _ALLOWED_IMPORTS or node.level:
                raise ObjectiveRejected(f"import from {node.module!r} is not allowed")
            for a in node.names:
                full = f"{node.module}.{a.name}"
                if full not in _ALLOWED_IMPORTS:
                    raise ObjectiveRejected(f"from-import of {full!r} is not allowed (import modules only)")
                aliases[a.asname or a.name] = full
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
            continue
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Expr) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Constant):
            continue                                          # a docstring / comment string
        else:
            raise ObjectiveRejected(f"module-level {type(node).__name__} at line {node.lineno}: "
                                    f"only imports and class definitions are allowed")
